headline: Orange Rain Warning Persists in Parts of Bataan and Zambales at 5 PM
seoTitle: Orange Rain Warning Persists in Parts of Bataan and Zambales
seoDescription: PAGASA kept parts of Bataan and Zambales under an Orange rainfall warning at 5 p.m. on August 14, while Metro Manila and nearby areas remained at Yellow level.
deck: PAGASA kept parts of Bataan and Zambales at Orange level at 5 p.m. Friday and maintained Yellow warnings over Metro Manila and nearby areas.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA's 5 p.m. rainfall advisory kept parts of Bataan and Zambales under an Orange warning, meaning flooding remained threatening in the listed localities.
The Orange coverage included Bagac, Mariveles, Morong, Limay, Orion, Pilar and Balanga in Bataan, and San Antonio, Subic and Olongapo in Zambales.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The 5 p.m. advisory placed Metro Manila and additional areas of Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan, Cavite and Batangas under a Yellow warning for flooding in flood-prone locations.

This is the same evolving weather event covered by FMB News' 7 a.m. report. The 1 p.m. delivery block was therefore merged into this canonical report instead of being published as a duplicate article.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Rainfall warning areas changed during the day, so residents and travelers needed the newest locality-level advisory rather than relying on the morning map. Low-lying communities and routes near waterways remained vulnerable to sudden flooding.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: PAGASA said the southwest monsoon would continue affecting Luzon and the western Visayas on August 15. Residents should monitor later PAGASA and local disaster-office advisories because warning coverage can narrow or expand quickly.
